title: The Laundry That Ran on Urine
summary: In a Pompeii fullery, you tread wool in tubs of stale urine, then rinse, brush, bleach it over sulphur and press it. Most fullers here were enslaved.

simplified: The worker is a composite. Recipes varied: urine, nitrum, potash and fuller's earth were all used, and no step-by-step manual survives. The order of washing, rinsing, drying, brushing, sulphur, earth and pressing follows Smith and Pliny and is the standard scholarly reading, not a recorded routine.
